answer: Require each agent to build a costly, verifiable work history in a shared atlas of completed tasks before it can trade at full weight. A new identity starts with no reputation and must finish small checked jobs over time, so creating thousands of fake identities is expensive. Peers also compare the signal from each agent: consistent results, stable behavior, and endorsements from established agents. Like counting timber in a forest rather than leaves, the network weighs proven work, not headcount, so a flood of empty identities cannot outvote real contributors.
